briefdescription.para: Execute a set of registered tasks respecting their dependency order.

detaileddescription.para: Execute DAG.

Tasks are executed in topological order derived from each task's dependencies list. Tasks whose dependencies have all succeeded are dispatched in parallel (up to max_concurrent_tasks). If a task fails, all tasks that (transitively) depend on it are skipped rather than executed. If a task's branch_condition predicate returns false, the task is condition-skipped and its dependents are condition-skipped transitively (reported in DagExecutionResult::condition_skipped).

task_ids
IDs of the tasks to include in this DAG execution. Tasks not in this set are ignored even if they appear in a dependency list.
DagExecutionResult with per-task outcomes (succeeded, failed, skipped, condition_skipped).
std::invalid_argument
if task_ids contains an unknown task ID.
std::runtime_error
if the dependency graph contains a cycle.
⚠️ SECURITY: This method MUST be protected by authentication and authorization.

briefdescription.para: Task scheduler for periodic execution of AQL queries and functions.

detaileddescription.para:
⚠️ SECURITY WARNING: This component executes arbitrary code and queries. Production deployments MUST implement:
RBAC - Only authorized users can register/modify tasks
Query validation - Sanitize AQL queries before execution
Resource limits - CPU time, memory, I/O quotas per task
Audit logging - Log all task operations (create, modify, execute, delete)
Isolation - Run tasks in sandboxed execution contexts
Encryption - Encrypt task definitions at rest if they contain sensitive data
Rate limiting - Prevent task flooding and abuse

Features:
Cron-like scheduling with configurable intervals
AQL query execution with full query engine integration
Custom function registration and execution
Task status monitoring and statistics
Graceful shutdown with running task completion
Concurrent task execution with resource limits
Task persistence (optional, for recovery after restart)

System Impact:
CPU: Minimal overhead for scheduler loop, actual impact depends on scheduled tasks
Memory: ~1KB per registered task, plus task execution memory
I/O: No direct I/O overhead, depends on executed queries/functions
Concurrency: Configurable max parallel tasks to limit resource usage
Write Path: No direct impact on write path, tasks run asynchronously

⚠️ SECURITY RISKS:
Arbitrary code execution via custom functions
SQL injection-like attacks via malicious AQL queries
Resource exhaustion (CPU, memory, disk) from malicious tasks
Privilege escalation if tasks run with elevated permissions
Data exfiltration via scheduled queries
DoS through task flooding or infinite loops
Sensitive data exposure in task definitions or logs
